summary: Both spectra are 2H-WS2 (E' ~355, A1' ~418-420, LA(M) ~176, 2LA(M) ~350, Si substrate 520.8-520.9). Spot 1 is thin and most consistent with a monolayer. Spot 2 is clearly thicker and multilayer. Raman alone does not prove spot 1 is a monolayer: the A1'-E' separation of 62.0 cm-1 sits at the monolayer end and is close to where a bilayer would fall, so a PL or low-wavenumber measurement is needed to rule out a bilayer.

observations.finding: Peak assignments. E' (in-plane E^1_2g, Gamma) at 355.29 (spot 1) and 355.38-355.5 (spot 2). A1' (out-of-plane A1g, Gamma) at 417.29 (spot 1) and 420.08 (spot 2). LA(M) at 176.0 and 175.6. Broad second-order 2LA(M) at 351.09 (spot 1) and 349.9-351.5 (spot 2). Si substrate TO at 520.91 and 520.80. Weak unlabelled features at 133, 304, 480, 594 cm-1 (spot 1) and a cluster around 140-320 and 460-585 cm-1 (spot 2) are at or near the noise floor and are not interpreted.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fits (lmfit) with linear baseline; fit residual RMS 11.5-13.9 counts vs point-to-point noise sigma 12.5-13.5 counts (from 540-580 cm-1). Fit errors on centres are ~0.01-0.3 cm-1. Two-component E-band fit preferred over one component: dBIC = 169 (spot 1) and 158 (spot 2).

observations.finding: A1'-E' separation is 62.0 cm-1 in spot 1 and 64.7 cm-1 in spot 2. This is the main thickness discriminator. Thin WS2 has a smaller separation and thicker WS2 a larger one, so spot 1 is thinner.
observations.evidence: 417.29 - 355.29 = 62.0 cm-1 (spot 1); 420.08 - 355.38 = 64.7 cm-1 (spot 2). Difference 2.7 cm-1. Fit uncertainty on each centre is ~0.05 cm-1; the separation is independent of the Si-based wavenumber offset because that offset cancels.

observations.finding: The A1' mode is 2.8 cm-1 lower in spot 1 (417.3 vs 420.1), while the E' mode is essentially unchanged (355.3 vs 355.4). The A1' stiffening with layer number in WS2 is the expected thickness trend. The unchanged E' argues against a large strain difference between the two spots.
observations.evidence: Delta(A1') = -2.79 cm-1; Delta(E') = -0.09 cm-1. Both fitted at 295 K.

observations.finding: The Si substrate peak is about 10x weaker on spot 2 than on spot 1. The thick WS2 region absorbs much more of the Si signal. A monolayer should attenuate the Si signal only slightly.
observations.evidence: Si integrated area 6762 (spot 1) vs 664 (spot 2), ratio 10.2. Si/A1' area ratio 1.19 vs 0.085 (14x). Peak-height and area estimates agree in direction; absolute attenuation depends on focus and is not calibrated here.

observations.finding: The 2LA(M) band is very strong relative to A1' in spot 1 and weak in spot 2. This is consistent with resonance enhancement at 514.5 nm (2.41 eV), which lies close to the WS2 B-exciton (~2.4-2.5 eV). The 2LA/A1' ratio is therefore not a clean thickness indicator.
observations.evidence: Area ratio 2LA/A1' = 4.4 (spot 1) vs 0.9-1.4 (spot 2). The spot 2 decomposition is unstable across fit starting points (2LA centre 349.9 vs 351.5 cm-1), so the spot 2 ratio is uncertain by roughly +/-30%. The spot 1 decomposition is stable.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013) for 2LA(M) assignment; Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013) for B-exciton energy (recalled, not verified here).

observations.finding: Crystal quality appears similar in both spots. E' and A1' linewidths barely differ, and there is no sign of a second crystal phase.
observations.evidence: FWHM(E') = 3.95 vs 4.12 cm-1; FWHM(A1') = 4.52 vs 4.40 cm-1. The LA(M)/A1' area ratio is higher in spot 1 (0.33 vs 0.12). This LA(M) increase could be resonance or defect activation and is not decisive.

observations.finding: The data do not show a monolayer-specific fingerprint beyond the A1'-E' separation and Si attenuation. A Raman-only assignment of spot 1 as 1L is therefore provisional.
observations.evidence: Separation 62.0 cm-1 is at the value often quoted for 1L WS2 (about 61-62 cm-1) and within about 1-2 cm-1 of few-layer values. Spectral resolution here is ~0.7 cm-1 per point, and wavenumber calibration uncertainty is ~0.2 cm-1.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), A1'-E' separation vs layer number (recalled from memory; verify the table/figure before quoting numbers).

caveats: Wavenumber calibration: the Si reference is at 520.91 (spot 1) and 520.80 (spot 2) vs the standard ~520.7 cm-1, so absolute frequencies may be offset by +0.1-0.2 cm-1. The A1'-E' separation is unaffected.

Spot size (~1 um) can mix the thin island with neighbouring SiO2 or thicker WS2, especially if spot 1 sits near an island edge. The strong Si signal (Si/A1' = 1.19) suggests substantial bare-substrate contribution, so spot 1 may not be a pure monolayer signal.
The Si attenuation argument is qualitative. Focus, objective NA and island height all change Si intensity, and no bare-SiO2/Si reference was supplied.

The 2LA(M) amplitude is resonance-enhanced and depends on exciton energy, which in turn depends on thickness, strain and doping. Attributing the spot 1 vs spot 2 2LA difference to thickness alone is not justified.

Laser power is unknown. Heating red-shifts A1' and E' and thin flakes on SiO2 heat differently, so part of the A1' shift could be thermal. The unchanged E' argues against a large heating effect but does not exclude it.

Literature values (A1'-E' separation per layer number, 2LA(M) assignment, B-exciton energy) are recalled from memory without internet access and must be verified against the cited papers before use. The numeric thresholds are the least certain part of this report.
The E-band decomposition in spot 2 is not robust (2LA centre 349.9-351.5 cm-1 and 2LA/A1' ratio 0.9-1.4 depending on starting values). The spot 1 decomposition is stable.
questions_for_user: Was a low-wavenumber spectrum taken (below 120 cm-1)? Monolayer WS2 has no interlayer shear or breathing modes, whereas bilayer shows a shear mode at roughly 20-30 cm-1. This would be the most direct test of 1L vs 2L with Raman. The current files start at 120 cm-1.

Do you have a photoluminescence spectrum for each spot? Monolayer WS2 shows strong direct-gap PL near 2.0 eV (~620 nm). A bilayer shows much weaker PL, and the spot 1 PL intensity relative to spot 2 would be strong evidence for a monolayer.
What AFM step height did you measure on the island? WS2 is about 0.6-0.7 nm per layer, so a height near 0.7 nm would confirm a monolayer.
What laser power, objective NA, grating and integration time were used? These determine heating and the reliability of intensity comparisons.
Where exactly was spot 1 relative to the island edge? Edge or substrate contributions could explain the strong Si signal and the large 2LA band.
Was a bare-substrate reference spectrum taken on the same day? That would calibrate the Si attenuation and the Si wavenumber offset.
citations: Berkdemir A. et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), 'Identification of individual and few layers of WS2 using Raman spectroscopy': E' and A1' assignments, A1'-E' separation vs layer number, and LA(M)/2LA(M) features at 514.5 nm. Recalled from memory; not verified here.

Zhao W. et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013), 'Evolution of electronic structure in atomically thin sheets of WS2 and WSe2': A and B exciton energies of WS2 layers, B exciton ~2.4 eV (near the 514.5 nm = 2.41 eV excitation). Recalled from memory; not verified here.
Temple P.A. & Hathaway C.E., Phys. Rev. B 7, 3685 (1973): Si Gamma-phonon reference near 520.7 cm-1 at room temperature. Recalled from memory; not verified here.
limits: Two spectra only (one spot each); no repeats, no spatial map, no PL, no AFM, no low-wavenumber data, no polarisation data, no laser power.
No calibrated thickness-vs-Si-attenuation relation was available, so the absolute layer count for spot 2 is not determined beyond 'multilayer'.
The A1'-E' separation thresholds for mono- and few-layer WS2 are literature recollections. The data alone cannot put spot 1 unambiguously at 1L rather than 2L.
No literature was accessed; the cited papers are referenced from memory. Work in the scratch folder was limited to fitting scripts; the data files were not modified.
